issue_context.title: API-server repair considers ports with same port number but different protocols as same
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
I created several Workloads which require up to ten ports for both UDP and TCP protocol. Now my logs get spammed with `the node port [PORT] for service [SERVER] was assigned to multiple services; please recreate`.

**What you expected to happen**:
[repair.go::collectServiceNodePorts](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/core/service/portallocator/controller/repair.go#L203) should consider `PORT-PROTO`-combination instead of only `PORT`.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Deploy any service with a node-port with both protocols, e.g.:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 30080
    targetPort: 80
    protocol: UDP
    name: dummy
  - port: 30080
    targetPort: 80
    protocol: TCP
    name: http
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:
This was already acknowledged by @thockin here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/59119#issuecomment-490760644
However, as this thread addresses a different bug and seems kind of stuck, i'd like to suggest that this might be addressed in a new context.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): `v1.17.5`
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: `Hetzner Cloud`
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): `Debian GNU/Linux 10 (buster)`
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): `Linux server 4.19.0-8-amd64 #1 SMP Debian 4.19.98-1+deb10u1 (2020-04-27) x86_64 GNU/Linux`
- Install tools: Deployed via Rancher v2.4.3

🤖 I am a bot run by vllry. 👩‍🔬
How did you get into this situation?  The allocator should not have granted the same node port twice?

Oh right, that issue.

The only real way out is to de-allocate the NodePorts and then re-allocate them, I think

As this happens for all of my ports in the said Production Application (the one where my log gets spammed) as well as complete fresh installation (where i verified the bug), i think there's no "way out" except fixing the bug.

As said, for me it's necessary to assign both protocols to the same port. This might be a niche-use-case, but checking the [List of TCP and UDP port numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_TCP_and_UDP_port_numbers) it's actually very likely for ports to allow tcp AND udp.

I'm not sure about the history of this, but it might be that issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/20092 was the origin, which was adressed in PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/30253 ("Allow services which use same port, different protocol to use the same nodePort for both"). But this PR doesn't contain the adjustment of the said [repair.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/core/service/portallocator/controller/repair.go), so repair.go still considers the behaviour as invalid, while it's actually allowed and supported.

Ahh, I thought you meant that you had accidentally been allocated the same nodePorts and I was very confused when you said "all of them".

I have reproduced this issue, and I can see it by inspection.

The obvious fix would be to collect ports split by protocol, but I think that's not right since we don't store it split. 

An even simpler fix would be for https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/core/service/portallocator/controller/repair.go#L203 to build a `map[protocol][]int`.  Then for each protocol, for each port, build `[]int` that contains all the port numbers, but remove any duplicates ONLY IF they are duplicated across protocols.  Duplicates in the same protocol should be retained (to report an error later).

I don't have time to tackle this tonight (and write a test), but it seems like a good bug.

perhaps I can fix this problem
/assign

@thockin things may be a little more complicated. 

Right now the [port allocator](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/83f343011f566130b813e81c84c40d218d10fecc/pkg/registry/core/service/portallocator/controller/repair.go#L125) is not aware of the protocol of the port https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/83f343011f566130b813e81c84c40d218d10fecc/pkg/registry/core/service/portallocator/controller/repair.go#L138

so I guess simply rewriting function `collectServiceNodePorts` to return `map[protocol][]int` is not enough, the port allocator will still return `portallocator.ErrAllocated` on same node port even with different protocol.

perhaps we need to refactor the `PortAllocator` to make it protocol-aware.

I don't think we need to do make the allocator be protocol aware.  IIRC we allow you to use the same nodeport on different protocols ONLY within a single service.

This means (I think) that we can do hyper-local deduplication as we collect the nodeports for each service.  If we find the same nodeport number with different protocols, just remove the duplicates because it is allowed.

I.e.  a service that looks like:
```
  ports:
  - name: a
    port: 53
    protocol: TCP
    nodePort: 30053
  - name: b
    port: 53
    protocol: UDP
    nodePort: 30053 # NOTE: same nodeport, different protocol
```

...would return `[]int{30053}` - deduped.

...but if ANY OTHER service tried to use 30053 it would be an error at the "rebuilt" allocator

Likewise if a single Service claims to use the same nodeport number more than once on the same protocol, it should be an error:

```
  ports:
  - name: a
    port: 53
    protocol: TCP
    nodePort: 30053
  - name: b
    port: 54
    protocol: TCP  # NOTE: same nodeport and protocol
    nodePort: 30053
```

...would return `[]int{30053, 30053}` - NOT deduped.
obviously, we want a great unit test here :P
@thockin ah got it! thanks for your detailed explanation!
